what_worked: Payment provider median comparison (slide 4) surfaced a genuinely interesting Superwall outlier observation.
fix_next: Replace decorative illustrations with real data charts; verify every claimed statistic against the dataset before presenting it as fact.
verdict: Mostly motivational filler with thin, often unverifiable data claims.
factual_error_detail: Slide 3: '68% under $1K/mo' — dataset has 216 zero-revenue rows (21.6%), but the 68% bucket is unverifiable and likely wrong given 30-day revenue figures not monthly. Slide 4: Stripe median $234 vs reference $234 is close but Stripe share stated as 60% when it's 636/1000=63.6%; Superwall median $4,159 vs reference ~$4,159 is plausible but labeled as $4.16k on chart. Slide 6: r=0.29 for Twitter followers vs revenue is unverifiable from the reference data and likely fabricated; '80% grew revenue faster than audience' is unsupported. Slide 8: '1 in 5 startups hide their identity' — anonymous companies are 129/1000=12.9%, not 20%. Slide 2: calls data 'audited' which overstates the dataset's nature.

evidence.insight: Superwall median observation (slide 4) is the only non-obvious finding. Most slides offer platitudes ('boring is profitable,' 'consistency beats virality') without analytical depth. No category analysis, no revenue concentration, no missingness discussion.
evidence.narrative: There is a loose arc from 'what is TrustMRR' to 'takeaways,' but the middle slides are loosely connected topics (providers, geography, followers, stealth companies, outliers) without a unifying thesis. The conclusion is generic motivational advice.
evidence.framing: No audience is defined. No research question is stated. Dataset limitations (24% missing country, 27% missing category, 29% missing audience_type) are never acknowledged. The dataset is called 'audited' without justification.
evidence.accuracy: Multiple fabricated or unverifiable statistics: 68% under $1K, r=0.29, 80% grew revenue faster, 1-in-5 stealth (actual 12.9%). Revenue distribution buckets are presented without showing methodology. The 30-day revenue figure is treated as monthly MRR without clarification. Missing Paddle and Lemon Squeezy from provider chart.
evidence.visual: Heavy reliance on decorative AI illustrations (slides 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10) that convey no data. Only one actual data chart (slide 4 bar chart). Slide 9 has garbled/corrupted text in the central graphic ('Romeri CAT,' 'Sone %0$'). Consistent dark theme but monotonous pink/purple palette with no visual variety in chart types.
evidence.ai_slop: Pervasive: every slide has a large decorative AI illustration; consulting-style motivational language ('The Anti-Hype Source,' 'The Winning Formula'); slide 9 contains visibly corrupted AI-generated graphic with nonsense text; generic three-column card layouts repeated on slides 7 and 11.
